text:
lena (Support): FYI Sparkline reported a customer-facing latency regression starting ~09:10 UTC. They want an SLA commitment but p95 doubled for their main route. attaching quick numbers.

carlos (Sales): customer is on an expansion plan, asking for a formal SLA before next renewal. Marking P0 for commercial reasons.

maya (PM): Can we confirm scope? Is this a model perf regression, routing/capacity, or config change? Need clear ask: temporary mitigation vs long-term fix.

sam (Eng Lead): Initial look at traces -> hotspot in token generation stage, spiking GPU compute at tail. Could be model variant or a batching/queueing shift.

jo (Oncall): From infra side, no recent infra deploys in that region until 08:55. Autoscaler did trigger more nodes at 09:05 then some backpressure at 09:12.

---LOG---
```
route: /v1/chat/sparkline
model: mosaic-v2-8k-quant
p50: 120ms -> 130ms
p95: 480ms -> 980ms
throughput: 120rps -> 90rps
errors: 0.2% -> 0.25%
```
---END---

lena (Support): customer says regression started after their traffic increased ~2x; they haven't changed prompts. They want a temporary SLA guarantee or mitigation now.

tina (SRE): Autoscaling logs show a short window of GPU saturation on pool `prod-west-2-gpu-4`. There was a backlog spike — queueing added latency. We could route them to a different pool but that may increase cost.

carlos (Sales): They'll accept a temporary routing workaround if we can promise 99th pct p95 under X ms for next 2 weeks. Need an answer today.

maya (PM): Options: 1) Short-term routing policy -> prefer mosaic-fast-4k for Sparkline (likely lower latency but lower context); 2) Reserve dedicated capacity for them (costly & longer); 3) Optimize batching/cache config (medium effort). We should pick mitigation + evaluation criteria for backlog.

sam (Eng Lead): Implementing a route override is fastest. Suggest add policy: if request.headers["x-customer"] == "sparkline" then route to `mosaic-fast-4k` with x-limit 250 tokens. Also enable prefix KV caching for this customer.

Code idea for routing rule:
```
route_rules:
  - match: x-customer == "sparkline"
    route: mosaic-fast-4k
    max_tokens: 250
    ttl_cache: 600s
```

jo (Oncall): I'll roll that as a canary to 5% of sparks immediately, watch p95, then ramp.

deploy-bot: roll initiated by jo: deploy/route-override-sparkline v1 -> canary 5%

(10m later)

jo (Oncall): Canary looks good. Sparkline p95 down to ~300ms for canary traffic. No errors.

maya (PM): Great. Short-term mitigation accepted by customer. Next: define long-term criteria. We need cost delta, SLA wording, and engineering estimate to fix root cause.

sam (Eng Lead): Root cause hypotheses: quantization regression for mosaic-v2-8k causing higher compute at long sequences OR batching policy change leading to head-of-line blocking. Need 2-day deep dive with perf tests.

tina (SRE): I'll run isolated perf runs on mosaic-v2-8k vs mosaic-fast-4k with varying sequence lengths and batch sizes. Estimate 1 day to get benchmarks.

carlos (Sales): Can we offer provisional SLA wording: "For route routing policy mosaic-fast-4k we can guarantee p95 < 400ms for typical Sparkline workload for a 14-day probation" — pending cost review?

maya (PM): We can commit to a provisional SLA if finance signs off on expected monthly cost delta. Product needs an acceptance criteria doc: launch when root-cause fix reduces p95 by >=30% for customer baseline and standard e2e tests pass.

Action items:
- jo (Oncall): finish canary -> full roll for policy if stable (due: +2h)
- tina (SRE): perf bench comparison mosaic-v2-8k vs mosaic-fast-4k (due: +1d)
- sam (Eng Lead): perf deep dive + list of possible fixes (quant params, batching, kernel selection) (due: +2d)
- maya (PM): create acceptance criteria doc + SLA draft for sales/legal (due: +1d)
- carlos (Sales): confirm customer OK with provisional routing workaround and cost tolerance (due: today EOD)

lena (Support): I'll update the customer and attach the canary dashboard link.

maya (PM): I'll slot this into the backlog and tag as customer-driven SLA initiative; priority: high - commercial. We'll revisit after perf results. :thumbsup:

sam (Eng Lead): Acknowledged. Starting investigation.

carlos (Sales): Thanks team. I'll push for provisional sign-off.

lena (Support): Customer updated, appreciative of quick mitigation. Keeping thread open for root-cause results.

(Last note)

deploy-bot: canary rolled to 100% after jo approval -> deploy/route-override-sparkline v1 -> stable

maya (PM): closing triage for now, will reopen if perf tests show otherwise.
